findings.title: Concurrent-deletion NPE fix is incomplete: subgroup listing overloads still dereference a null model
findings.body: getSubGroupsCount() was changed to tolerate modelSupplier.get() returning null (the case where the cached GroupAdapter is still usable while the group has already been removed from the database), but the three sibling overloads were not fixed: getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults) at line 262 and getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults) at line 268 all still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. Under the same race that motivated this PR (cached group visible while concurrently deleted), these methods throw a NullPointerException, so the reported concurrent-access NPE is only fixed for the subgroup-count path, not for the subgroup listing endpoints that use the very same supplier. Apply the same null handling to those overloads (e.g. return Stream.empty() / a null-aware result or fall back consistently) rather than patching only one call site.

findings.title: Background reader thread is never joined and can hang the test JVM or let the assertion race
findings.body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a non-daemon reader thread (new Thread(...).start() at line 139) and only stops it by setting deletedAll in the normal path; there is no try/finally. If anything in the deletion loop throws (e.g. an admin DELETE returns an error) or the test aborts before line 155, deletedAll is never set, so the loop keeps issuing groups() requests forever and the non-daemon thread prevents the test JVM from exiting. In addition, the assertion assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()) at line 157 executes immediately after deletedAll.set(true) without joining the reader, so a read that is still in flight can record its exception after the assertion runs, allowing a regression to pass unnoticed. The thread should be stopped in a finally block, joined before the assertion, and ideally created as a daemon.
